experiment.name: geolocation_500
experiment.question: Does a single-shot generative privacy edit stop four independent VLMs from geolocating a street scene, and by how much?
experiment.metric: great-circle error in km between the model's guess and the Cityscapes GPS ground truth (haversine, R = 6371.0 km). Higher is better protection.
experiment.image_set: 500 Cityscapes frames, 25 from each of 20 cities, pinned by readydata/dataset_random_500/metadata/dataset.json and reproduced in index.csv. It is the 100-image set of results/geolocation_100/ plus 400 additions (benchmark/datasetup/build_cityscapes_500.py); the two halves are disjoint and their union is exactly these 500.
experiment.contents: VLM reasoning responses only. No images are included.

design.what_is_present: the unprotected reference and the GPT Image 2 baseline, each read by all four evaluators. Nothing else has been run on this image set.

source_run.evaluation: <dataset>/evaluation/<run>/<image_set>/<provider>/<model>/results.json - a positional array of responses with no image id

alignment.rule: results.json stores responses positionally. Slot i belongs to image i of the manifest named in that run's archived experiment_config.yaml - dataset.json for the 100-image half, dataset_new400.json for the 400-image half. Every list length matched its manifest exactly; nothing was guessed.
alignment.one_run_without_a_config: dataset_random_100/evaluation/gpt_image_100_20260813_122752 predates configs being archived. Its lists are 100 long, which matches dataset.json exactly, so the fallback is unambiguous.
alignment.union_rule: A variant's answers are unioned by image_id across every matching run and any non-null answer wins - the same rule as benchmark/analysis/merge_gpt_image_500.py, which produces the merged 500-image aggregate from these same archives.
alignment.excluded: dataset_random_100/evaluation/gpt_image_10_20260813_103949, a 10-image smoke run over a subset of the 100 that is fully covered by the 100-image run.

source_run.note: Response bodies are the source objects verbatim, deep-equality checked, re-serialised one file per image because the source keeps them in a single positional array.

baseline_under_test.name: GPT Image 2
baseline_under_test.what: one single-shot image edit per photograph, from a fixed prompt - no reasoning stage, no grounding, no iteration. It is the closest thing here to 'just ask a good image model to remove the location'.
baseline_under_test.prompt: prompts/geolocation/defense_image_edit_prompt.txt in this repository, byte-identical to the file the attack ran (4209 characters as the run recorded it)

resolution_confound.why_it_matters: The defended image is not the same size as the original. Every evaluator read a smaller picture in the gpt-image condition than in the raw condition, and the perceptual metrics compare a resized pair. Some part of the measured protection is resolution loss rather than content removal, and nothing in this run separates the two.

evaluators.role: All four are independent scorers. None of them is inside a protection loop, because no protection loop was run on this image set - so unlike results/geolocation_100/, every number here is a transfer number.
evaluators.prompt_note: This is the benchmark's own attacker prompt, and it is NOT the same file as prompts/geolocation/attack_base_prompt.txt at the top of this repository, which is the pipeline's. The benchmark prompt asks only for reasoning and a location estimate, which is why these responses carry two keys and no critical_features.

process.why: No VeilLens protection run covers this image set. The largest Cityscapes geolocation run on disk is 100 images (pipeline2/result/test_iter3), whose ids are exactly the 100-image half of this set and whose reasoning is archived in full at results/geolocation_100/. See process/PENDING.json.
process.consequence: Nothing in this folder measures VeilLens on 500 images. Everything here is the GPT Image 2 baseline and the unprotected reference.

response_schema.note: Exactly the two keys of prompts/eval_schema.json - checked on all 4000 files. No critical_features and no image_path: the benchmark's attacker prompt does not ask for them. Which image each response read is fixed by its filename, which comes from the positional alignment above.

unscored.note: Every one of the 4,000 calls in the matrix returned a scored answer. The gemini-3.1-pro-preview quota gap that shaped the first build was closed by backfill chunks c2, k2 and d; the two gemini-3-flash-preview failures were retried in chunk e.

perceptual_metrics.what: image-quality metrics for the GPT Image 2 edit against the unmodified frame. Computed by the evaluation runner, not by a VLM.
perceptual_metrics.ssim_correction: The 100-image half was computed under Python 3.14 + numpy 2.2.6, which silently corrupts skimage's SSIM above 256 KiB - its archived ssim_mean reads 37.5, impossible for a bounded metric. Those 100 values are replaced by the recompute in dataset_random_100/evaluation/ssim_recomputed_numpy2.3.5.json; the archived value is kept beside each as ssim_archived, and ssim_source says which is which.

checks.check: the image set is the pinned 500 and each half is scored against its own manifest
every emitted response parses as JSON, carries a non-empty 'reasoning', and has exactly the keys of prompts/eval_schema.json
recomputed haversine(ground truth, location_estimate) equals the recorded error
every unscored cell is a recorded API failure in the source, not a dropped file
checks.result: 0 unscored, all carrying the source's error string; 4000 - 4000 = 0

checks.check: perceptual_metrics.json covers every image pair and no SSIM exceeds 1.0
index.csv lists the 500 images once, in dataset.json order
every index.csv error cell equals the recorded prediction_errors_km
checks.result: 4000 populated cells, 0 mismatches (exact, full round-trip precision)

checks.check: index.csv n_responses equals the response files on disk
emitted bodies are deep-equal to the source objects
each summary.json recomputes from the response files beside it
each run's mean and count reproduce that run's own summary.json
index.csv ground-truth coordinates equal dataset.json exactly
results/geolocation_100/ covers exactly the 100-image half of this set

index_csv.rows: 500, one per image, in dataset.json order

columns.in_geolocation_100: yes if the image is also in results/geolocation_100/
columns.n_responses: how many of the eight filled cells hold a response for this image (0-8)
columns.<condition>_<model>_error_km: verbatim from prediction_errors_km in the source results.json; blank means the API call failed
columns.ssim, lpips, clip_iqa_diff, liqe_diff: from perceptual_metrics.json - the GPT Image 2 edit against the unmodified frame; ssim for the first 100 is the corrected recompute

index_csv.blank_cells: mean the API call failed, never that a file was dropped.
index_csv.not_included: location_estimate.confidence, which would add eight more columns. It is in every response file.
